newsitem.title: UK: Alliance & Leicester firms after auction.
newsitem.headline: Alliance & Leicester firms after auction.

text.p: Shares in Alliance & Leicester Plc were up 20-1/2p to 553-1/2p by 0810 GMT as some institutional players began to scramble for shares they failed to pick up during the three-day auction process, dealers said.
"Institutions need to take more stock on board so I suspect we will see a bit of a push this morning," the head of sales and trading at a major brokerage said.
The Alliance & Leicester said on Wednesday that the average price of Tuesday's third and final auction of free shares belonging to members was just over 528 pence.
A total of about 157 million shares were on offer after almost 27 percent of Alliance members opted to sell their free share allocation.
Alliance & Leicester shares made a sparkling debut on Monday, closing at 566-1/2p, well above market expectations.
"I'm not so sure we will see the shares that high today -- it really depends on how hungry the institutions are," one senior dealer said.
"There are other building societies to be floated in the next few months. But, unlike the Halifax, the Alliance is seen as a bid target."
The Halifax Building Society, Britain's biggest, is due to convert to a bank and join the London stock market on June 2.
